threads.body: [Style] Test code should not add `@Nullable`. The overridden base declaration already documents that this argument may be null, so remove the annotation here.

Clearing captured data inside every Awaitility attempt makes the immediately following `metrics()` check vacuous: `clearData()` explicitly guarantees that `metrics()` is empty until the next export, so this can pass even when the pool callbacks were not unregistered. Clear once, then wait for a subsequent metric collection (for example, retain the per-metric `waitAndAssertMetrics(..., isEmpty)` checks) so the cleanup assertions can detect leaked callbacks.

[Style] `VirtualField` handles count as constant-like values in the style guide, so this field should be `SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE`. Renaming it to `GENERATED_POOL_NAME_FIELD` (and updating the three usages below) would match how the other instrumentation modules declare their virtual fields.

[General] In HikariCP's `dataSourceClassName` configuration mode there is normally no `jdbcUrl` at all (Hikari warns and ignores one if it is set), so `getJdbcUrl()` is null here. `JdbcConnectionUrlParser.parse()` returns `DbInfo.DEFAULT` immediately for a null URL without ever consulting `props`, so the standard `serverName`/`portNumber`/`databaseName` entries in `getDataSourceProperties()` are dropped and every such pool derives `hikaricp`. The derived name is then not just uninformative but shared: those pools report distinct `HikariPool-N` values in `pool.name` today, and afterwards they would all report `hikaricp`. Falling back to the standard data source properties when the URL is absent would close the gap.

`shouldUseDataSourcePropertiesForDefaultPoolName` doesn't cover this, since it injects a `DataSource` instance and supplies a synthetic `jdbc:postgresql:ignored` URL — HikariCP ignores `dataSourceProperties` entirely in that branch.
